title: Copilot Studio: interactive MCP apps render inside agent conversations
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents Copilot Credits consumption for the Microsoft Copilot harness, including MCP tools, so the briefing incorrectly treats billing as unconfirmed and costs as staff time only. The data-policy instructions omit the connector action menu, and the briefing overstates whether general MCP controls stop app-originated calls.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No admin switch specific to MCP apps rendering is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCP apps" "admin" "setting"'; '"Copilot Studio" "MCP apps" tenant default disable admin switch'. Opened MCP apps, server setup, Agent 365 management and Tools overview; no app-rendering switch found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not separately stated a tenant-level MCP apps default beyond the roadmap's connection-based description.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Studio" "MCP apps" tenant default disable admin switch'. Read the roadmap, MCP apps page and Microsoft Copilot harness server setup; no separate tenant-level rendering default found.

claims.claim: The licensing model for this capability is unknown and not yet published.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself. Any experience that uses one of these consumes credits.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'consumption'. Replace licensing.notes with: 'Microsoft Copilot harness experiences consume Copilot Credits for LLM tokens, tools including MCPs, and the harness. A separate MCP app-rendering rate is not documented.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview to sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a separate licence specifically named for MCP apps.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio MCP apps billing Copilot Credits tool calls agent action licensing'; '"Copilot Studio" "MCP apps" "licensing" "rate"'. Read MCP apps and both harness billing pages; no separate MCP apps licence found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate fixed Copilot Credits rate for rendering an MCP app is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Studio" "MCP apps" "licensing" "rate"'; 'Copilot Studio MCP apps billing Copilot Credits tool calls agent action licensing'. Read MCP apps, Billing rates and management, and Overview of usage-based billing; no separate render rate found.

claims.claim: The Billing rates and management table lists Agent action at 5 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Agent action^4^ | 5 Copilot Credits | No charge |
claims.fix: Narrow the sentence to: 'For the standard harness, the Billing rates and management table lists Agent action at 5 Copilot Credits, with a No charge column for qualifying Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed usage; Microsoft Copilot harness agents are billed differently.' Do not use this table to establish an MCP apps tool-call rate.

claims.claim: Whether tool calls made from an MCP app consume Copilot Credits is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself. Any experience that uses one of these consumes credits.
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-tool-call statement with: 'For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Microsoft documents Copilot Credits consumption for tools including MCPs, as well as LLM tokens and the harness. A separate app-rendering rate is not documented.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview. Narrow the corresponding Open questions bullet to the separate app-rendering rate.

claims.claim: Cost is low because the only documented cost is maker and administrator time.
claims.quote: Briefing: 'The only cost shown is admin and maker time.' Microsoft: 'Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.'
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with: 'Variable. Microsoft Copilot harness experiences consume Copilot Credits for LLM tokens, MCP tools and the harness; a separate MCP app-rendering rate is not documented.' Retain maker and administrator time as indirect costs.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator blocks an MCP server at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Registry** tab.
3. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.
4. Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: An API equivalent of the registry's server-blocking control is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com graph API MCP server block unblock registry agent365 tools'. Read Agent 365 management and Tools overview plus Azure API Management governance search passages; no equivalent registry blocking API found.

claims.claim: Blocking a server disables all the tools it exposes.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.

claims.claim: The server block is organisation-wide in its supported management route, without establishing effects across all products or dependent components.
claims.quote: Select **Block** to restrict the server across your organization, or **Unblock** to restore access to a previously blocked server.

claims.claim: Individual MCP tools are managed at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled or Disabled toggle > Save.
claims.quote: Select the **Tools** tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an **Enabled** or **Disabled** toggle.

claims.claim: An API equivalent of the individual-tool registry toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com graph API MCP server individual tools enabled disabled policy'. Read Agent 365 management and Azure API Management control-access search passages; no equivalent registry tool-toggle API found.

claims.claim: Tool-level control is rolling out and supports only specific MCP server types registered on Agent 365.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: MCP registration requests are approved or rejected at Agents > Tools > Requests (preview) > request > Approve or Reject.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Tools**, and then select the **Requests (preview)** tab. ... Select **Approve** to make the server available in the organizational registry, or **Reject** to deny the request.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for approving or rejecting these MCP server registration requests is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com graph API MCP server registration request approve reject'. Read Agent 365 management, Tools overview and BYO approval search passages; no corresponding registration-approval API found.

claims.claim: AI Administrator and Global Administrator meet both requirements to complete review and approval.
claims.quote:
Two roles meet both requirements:

- AI Administrator.
- Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra consent is a separate step after server approval, required before availability to agent-building surfaces.
claims.quote: After approval, consent to the Microsoft Entra permissions required by the MCP server. The server becomes available to agent-building surfaces only after consent is granted.

claims.claim: The data-policy path goes directly from selecting the connector to Block.
claims.quote:
Select the three dots (**⋮**) next to the connector, and then:

- To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select **Block**.
claims.fix: Insert 'three dots (...)' between 'connector' and 'Block' in controls[3].ui.path and the rendered row. Add the completion instruction: 'Select Next, define scope if prompted and select Next, then review and select Create policy to apply the new policy.' The cited page documents these steps.

claims.claim: Get-DlpPolicy from Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell retrieves tenant policies and does not change connector classification.
claims.quote: The Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet retrieves policy objects for the logged in admin's tenant.

claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: The data-policy page does not explicitly mention MCP apps.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCP apps" "admin" "setting"'. Opened Configure data policies for agents and Add tools to custom agents; their MCP coverage describes connector/server tools, not MCP app rendering.

claims.claim: Data policies govern agents in the environments covered by the policy.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.claim: Administrators manage plugins and their skills and MCP servers in Microsoft 365 admin center, while Power Platform data policies control tool addition in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Admins manage plugins, including the skills and MCP servers they contain, in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Power Platform data policies still control which tools makers can add in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls, and an Agent 365 block need not apply across products.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components. An approval or block doesn't necessarily apply across all products or connected components.

claims.claim: General MCP server controls apply to these apps, so disabling a tool on a supporting server prevents an app from reaching it.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCP apps" "admin" "setting"'; 'graph API MCP server individual tools enabled disabled policy'. Read MCP apps and Agent 365 management; gateway enforcement is qualified to supported calling experiences, without confirming MCP apps.
claims.fix: In the summary replace 'but MCP server controls apply' with 'general MCP server controls exist, but Microsoft has not confirmed their applicability to app-originated calls'. Replace the At rollout tool-control bullet with: 'Consider disabling write, delete or payment tools where both the server type and calling experience support tool-level enforcement; confirm whether MCP app-originated calls use that enforcement route.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: '"Copilot Studio" "MCP apps" "identity" authentication'. Read MCP apps Security and access and Microsoft Copilot harness server setup; they describe configured authentication and server-dependent connections, not a single app-call execution identity.
